GENERATIVE RECONSTRUCTION

What actually ran

LOCAL GPU · NO EXTERNAL IMAGE API
PRETRAINED · MEDICAL CT

QDM-L diffusion

A 692-million-parameter diffusion transformer with a medical VAE. The official ×4 checkpoint was trained on head-and-neck CT from HaN-Seg and SegRap2023; this pilot transfers it to coronal reconstruction.

15 diffusion steps · fixed checkpoint
Official model & weights ↗
PRETRAINED · OUT OF DOMAIN

Real-ESRGAN ×4plus

An adversarially trained 16.7-million-parameter RRDB generator. Its natural-image training makes it an exploratory control, not a CT-specific model. Inspect raw output and withheld-slice errors.

GAN generator · no medical fine-tuning
Official model & weights ↗
PRETRAINED · OUT OF DOMAIN

Real-ESRNet ×4plus

The non-adversarial, pixel-loss-trained counterpart to Real-ESRGAN. The same RRDB architecture gives a useful control for the effects of adversarial training.

Reconstruction network · no medical fine-tuning

The earlier custom 3D neural priors and their two-seed ensemble remain in the viewer. They are separate from the pretrained models and are not included in this withheld-slice benchmark.
Reconstruction protocol & data provenance ＋

Source: BHSD label_192/images NIfTI volumes, matched to local RSNA labels. Header geometry has not been independently verified against the original DICOMs. All four examples are hemorrhage-positive.

Geometry: RAS canonical orientation, full affine retained (including tilt), resampled to a patient-coordinate grid retaining native X/Y spacing (approximately 0.488 mm), with 1.25 mm superior–inferior sampling. Every acquired 512 × 512 axial sample is retained for every method and the source view. Coronal images are displayed with their physical aspect ratio.

Conventional methods: SciPy nearest neighbor (order 0), trilinear (order 1), and cubic B-spline (order 3). Cubic interpolation can overshoot. Values outside the acquired volume are masked.

Earlier custom generative fit: 3D convolutional decoder, fixed random input, 42,417 parameters, Adam at 0.003, 350 iterations per seed (88 and 123), intensity-weighted source loss and a small through-plane smoothness penalty. The generator is fitted in the −100 to 200 HU range; residual projection then restores the full-range source intensities. Generated values between planes are model estimates. Neural outputs are fitted at four times the native slice sampling, then mapped to the same display grid.

Pretrained adapter: Each of the 512 native-grid coronal planes is processed independently, with grayscale repeated across RGB channels and a fixed −100 to 200 HU window. The ×4 result is area-reduced along X and aligned to acquired slice centers along Z. QDM uses overlapping 128-pixel tiles, repeated reflection padding, the official 15-step schedule and quadtree threshold 0.15. No weights are locally trained or fine-tuned. The released QDM inference documentation does not specify a HU preprocessing window; our chosen window is an additional transfer assumption.

Raw vs corrected: “Preserve acquired samples” adds a linearly interpolated residual computed only from available axial planes. Disable it to inspect raw model output. The displayed 2D methods have no explicit three-dimensional consistency constraint; inspect scrolling for flicker.

Withholding: Even axial planes are retained; interior odd planes are withheld from both model inputs and residual correction. The final unbracketed odd plane, if present, is excluded. The pretrained models were not tuned using these references. Scores use floating-point outputs before the viewer’s int16 quantization.

Limits: The correction preserves full-range source values under a point-sampling approximation. It does not model slice averaging, noise, or the CT reconstruction kernel. No genuinely missing-plane ground truth or clinical validation is available. Withheld acquired slices and BHSD hemorrhage-region intensity error provide a limited proxy test; they do not measure diagnostic sensitivity or lesion preservation. Seed disagreement and AI-versus-linear differences are exploratory, not error maps.

Reproducibility: Local preparation script, fit logs, seed outputs, affines, and metadata are retained with the dashboard. Study metadata can be downloaded from the sidebar.
